paragraphs: Fluence Energy, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), was initially formed on June 21, 2021 and completed its initial public offering (the "IPO") on November 1, 2021. We conduct our business operations through Fluence Energy, LLC and its direct and indirect subsidiaries. Fluence Energy, LLC was formed on June 30, 2017 as a joint venture between Siemens Industry, Inc. ("Siemens Industry"), an indirect subsidiary of Siemens AG ("Siemens"), and AES Grid Stability, LLC ("AES Grid Stability"), an indirect subsidiary of The AES Corporation ("AES"), and commenced operations on January 1, 2018. We refer to Siemens Industry and AES Grid Stability as the "Founders" in this Annual Report and together with Qatar Holding LLC ("QHL"), an affiliate of the Qatar Investment Authority ("QIA"), they are collectively referred to as the "Continuing Equity Owners." As the sole managing member of Fluence Energy, LLC, Fluence Energy, Inc. operates and controls all the business and affairs of Fluence Energy, LLC and its direct and indirect subsidiaries. As a result, Fluence Energy, Inc. consolidates Fluence Energy, LLC and records a non-controlling interest in its consolidated financial statements for the economic interest in Fluence Energy, LLC held by the Founders. Except where the content clearly indicates otherwise, any reference in this Annual Report to "Fluence," "we," "us," "our" or "the Company" refers to Fluence Energy, Inc. and all of its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Fluence Energy, LLC.

Fluence is a global market leader delivering intelligent energy storage and optimization software for renewables and storage. Our energy storage solutions and operational services are designed to help create a more resilient grid and unlock the full potential of renewable portfolios.

As of September 30, 2025, we had 6.8 gigawatts ("GW") of energy storage assets deployed and 9.1 GW of contracted backlog across 33 markets in 25 countries with a gross global pipeline of 128.8 GW. As of September 30, 2025, our global operational and maintenance ("O&M") services team was providing services for 5.6 GW of energy storage assets, with a further 7.0 GW of contracted backlog. As of September 30, 2025, we had an aggregate of 22.0 GW of renewable energy assets using Fluence digital offerings and 12.1 GW of contracted backlog related to renewable and energy storage assets using Fluence digital offerings.

The utility-scale battery storage industry continues to experience unprecedented growth fueled by (i) the global transition toward renewable energy, (ii) heightened focus on grid resilience, (iii) declining lithium-ion battery prices, (iv) increased electricity demand, and (v) supportive regulatory frameworks.
We believe the energy storage market is comprised of three main elements:

•Energy storage solutions — the components (including batteries), professional services, and labor required to manufacture, assemble, and install energy storage systems. The energy storage solutions market is driven by the deployment of new energy storage solutions globally and its addressable market is comprised of the annual spend associated with the manufacturing, delivery, and installation of new energy storage solutions. BloombergNEF estimated in its 2H 2025 Energy Storage Market Outlook published on October 20, 2025 that the global utility scale market, excluding China, will add approximately 3,201 GWh between 2024 and 2035.

•Services — recurring O&M services that energy storage solutions require and asset management services that are provided by third parties when asset owners outsource the operations of their systems. The services market element is driven by growth in installed energy storage solutions globally and its addressable market is comprised of the recurring annual service spend across the entire fleet of energy storage projects, which continues to grow through new installations.

•Digital applications and software — cloud-based software that help asset owners optimize the performance of their systems and portfolios, including asset performance management ("APM") software and intelligent forecasting and bid optimization software for asset trading applications. Cloud-based software applications can be deployed on both energy storage assets and renewable assets. The digital applications sector is driven by the growth in installed energy storage solutions and renewable assets, and its addressable market is comprised of the total global installed fleet of energy storage solutions and renewable assets. We believe there is an opportunity to not only deploy digital offerings and software solutions on individual assets but also across entire energy storage fleets and portfolios of generation assets to improve both performance and economic output, as well as to reduce the total cost of ownership ("TCO") of the asset with improvements in both service productivity and with
enhanced predictive maintenance, and the opportunity to reduce the overall carbon footprint of the portfolio by optimizing various asset types.
As described above, we believe there are multiple key factors driving continued growth in the energy storage sector, including, but not limited to:

•Global Transition Toward Renewable Energy: The ongoing transition from fossil to renewable generation is expected to continue to require significant increases in energy storage capacity to both offset potential grid instability caused by intermittent renewable resources and enable the use of power from renewable generation assets at times when natural resources may be unavailable. Energy storage will be essential in managing variations in renewable electricity output.

•Grid Resilience: Growing capacity constraints on existing power grids that were not designed to support distributed and renewable generation infrastructure or technologies, such as electric vehicles, position energy storage assets as a key solution.

•Declining Lithium-Ion Battery Prices: Growth of the industry and the continued adoption of energy storage solutions by our customers is driven by the declining cost of the lithium-ion energy storage hardware, mainly the cost of lithium-ion batteries. The cost of lithium-ion energy storage hardware has declined significantly in the last decade and has resulted in a large addressable market today. In fiscal year 2022, we saw prices for lithium-ion batteries increase from prior years, though prices returned to their historical trend of declining year-over-year in fiscal years 2023 through 2025, due in part to manufacturing overcapacity and saturation in the market and lower cost of the underlying raw materials, including lithium as well as softening demand from the electric vehicle ("EV") sector. The market for energy storage continues to rapidly evolve and while we believe lithium-ion battery costs will continue to decline over the long-term, they may not decline or decline at the rates we expect. If costs do not continue to decline long-term and instead remain steady or increase, as seen in fiscal year 2022, this could adversely affect demand for our products and services, our revenue, order intake, our market share, and ability to grow our business.

•Increased Electricity Demand: Driven by factors such as the rise of data centers and AI. The surge in demand for electricity increases the need for energy storage systems to ensure grid stability, manage peak loads and provide reliability to power grids, especially during periods of elevated use. There is significant need for technology solutions that can be deployed in the next 5 years to keep up with AI data center build out and energy storage is well suited to be deployed at scale in this timeline. According to a publication from the U.S. Department of Energy in April 2024, electricity demand is forecasted to grow substantially in the United States over the next decade. This is being driven to some extent by data centers and AI, in another report by the U.S. Department of Energy in December 2024, data centers are expected to consume approximately 6.7% to 12% of total U.S. electricity by 2028. We are seeing similar trends of increasing electricity demand in other countries, including those in which we operate.

You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information set forth in this Annual Report, including Part II, Item 7. See "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" above.

Our business and customer demand for our offerings depends in part on government incentives and/or regulations relating to or mandating the use of renewable energy and/or energy storage. Changes or potential changes to government incentives or regulations has and could in the future impact demand for our energy storage solutions, which could lead to adverse effects to our business, operating results, and cash flows.

Federal, state, local, and foreign government bodies provide incentives and/or regulations relating to mandating or encouraging use of renewable energy and/or energy storage to owners, end users, distributors, system integrators, and manufacturers of renewable energy and energy storage products and solutions to promote renewable electricity and energy storage in the form of rebates, tax credits, other financial incentives, procurement requirements and market structures. The range and duration of these incentives and regulations varies widely by jurisdiction and type of asset involved. Our customers typically use our energy storage solutions for grid-connected applications wherein power is sold under a power purchase agreement or into an organized electric market. The reduction, elimination, modification, expiration, or determination of inapplicability of government incentives or regulations related to mandating or encouraging the use of grid-connected renewable electricity and/or energy storage or the potential of any such reduction, elimination, modification, expiration, or determination of inapplicability of government incentives or regulations has and may in the future negatively affect the competitiveness of our offerings the growth of our industry and our business. Such government incentives and/or regulations may expire on a particular date, end when the allocated funding is exhausted or be reduced or terminated as renewable energy adoption rates increase or as a result of legal challenges, changing policies or priorities, the adoption of new statutes or regulations or changes to existing regulations, new regulatory guidance, or the passage of time. Reductions, modification, terminations, or determination of inapplicability of government incentives and/or regulations may occur without warning. Such policies, regulations, and incentives may not continue to exist in current form, or at all. The reduction, modification, elimination, or expiration or the potential of any such reduction, elimination, modification, expiration, of such government incentives or regulations or determination of inapplicability of such government incentives or regulations has impacted and may in the future impact customer demand for our offerings, may lead to a loss of customers and potential customer projects, and has and may in the future harm our business, operating results, and cash flows. From time to time, we may pursue acquisitions or other strategic transactions in order to take advantage of potential incentives. However, any such acquisition or transaction may not be consummated on the timeline we expect or at all, and it may not achieve its intended benefits.

For example, in August 2022, the United States passed the IRA, which included incentives that supported the adoption of energy storage solutions, including a new "technology neutral" Section 48E investment tax credit (the "ITC") and Section 45Y production tax credit (the "PTC"), changes to the previous Section 48 non-"technology neutral" investment tax credit and Section 45 production tax credit, and the Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Tax Credit (the "AMPC"). On July 4, 2025, the OBBBA was signed into law, which significantly modified certain provisions of the IRA, including those related to energy storage. The OBBBA supports energy storage in the United States, as the bill includes long-term continued availability of the ITC for energy storage projects and the AMPC for domestically manufactured cells, modules, and inverters in energy storage systems. Certain tax credits, notably including the ITC for energy storage, will begin to phase down for projects that start construction (in accordance with Internal Revenue Service ("IRS") guidance) after 2033. The prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements enacted under the IRA continue to apply under the OBBBA for the project owner to receive the full ITC value, and the credit value can be further increased if the project owner also qualifies for a domestic content bonus credit and energy communities bonus credit. The OBBBA amended the provisions of the domestic content bonus credit for the ITC such that the project owner now must achieve higher minimum domestic content percentage thresholds. In addition, the OBBBA amended the ITC and AMPC establishing new Prohibited Foreign Entity ("PFE") restrictions.

The new PFE restrictions apply to virtually all key tax credits under the IRA and come in two forms: (i) for tax years beginning after July 4, 2025, the taxpayer taking the ITC and AMPC tax credit cannot not be a PFE and (ii) for ITC projects that start construction in 2026 and after, and AMPC eligible components that are made and sold in the manufacturing facility's tax year that begins after July 4, 2025, the ITC eligible project or AMPC eligible component must source a certain percentage of material from non-PFEs (known as "material assistance"), and the percentage of material from non-PFEs increases annually over time. The OBBBA includes substantive details regarding PFE restriction compliance requirements and requires U.S. Department of Treasury to issue implementation regulations by December 31, 2026. There is continuing uncertainty on certain aspects of the IRA and related guidance, the OBBBA and forthcoming related guidance (including with respect to PFE restrictions). In the past such uncertainty related to the IRA caused certain customers to take an extended period to evaluate, negotiate, and enter energy storage arrangements, which has impacted our business and results of operations. Current uncertainty related to changes imposed by the OBBBA may in the future

similarly cause customers to delay contracting decisions or may cause customers to delay or cancel existing projects as they navigate such uncertainty, which could have a material negative effect on our business and results of operations.

paragraphs: Fluence Energy, Inc., 一間設立於德國特拉華州的公司（the "Company"），最初於2021年6月21日成立，並於2021年11月1日完成首次公開發行（the "IPO"）。我們透過Fluence Energy, LLC及其直接與間接子公司進行業務運作。Fluence Energy, LLC於2017年6月30日成立，為西門子工業公司（"Siemens Industry"），為西門子AG（"Siemens"）間接子公司，與AES Grid Stability, LLC（"AES Grid Stability"），為AES Corporation（"AES"）間接子公司所共同成立的合資企業，並於2018年1月1日開始營運。我們在本年度報告中將Siemens Industry與AES Grid Stability稱為"Founders"，並與卡塔爾持有公司（"QHL"），為卡塔爾投資局（"QIA"）之關係企業， collectively referred to as the "Continuing Equity Owners." 作為Fluence Energy, LLC唯一管理成員，Fluence Energy, Inc.運作並控制Fluence Energy, LLC及其直接與間接子公司的所有業務與事務。因此，Fluence Energy, Inc.將Fluence Energy, LLC合併入帳，並於其合併財務報表中記錄非控制權益，反映Founders所持有的Fluence Energy, LLC經濟權益。除非內容明確另有說明，否則本年度報告中任何提及"Fluence"、"we"、"us"、"our"或"the Company"均指Fluence Energy, Inc.及其所有直接與間接子公司，包括Fluence Energy, LLC。
Fluence為全球市場領導者，提供智能能源儲存與可再生能源及儲能優化軟體。我們的能源儲存解決方案與運營服務旨在協助建立更強韌的電網，並發揮可再生能源組合的全部潛力。

截至2025年9月30日，我們已部署6.8 gigawatts（"GW"）的能源儲存資產，並在25個國家的33個市場擁有9.1 GW的合約待履行訂單，全球總體儲備為128.8 GW。截至2025年9月30日，我們的全球運營與維護（"O&M"）服務團隊為5.6 GW的能源儲存資產提供服務，另有7.0 GW的合約待履行訂單。截至2025年9月30日，我們總共有22.0 GW的可再生能源資產使用Fluence數位服務，並有12.1 GW的合約待履行訂單與使用Fluence數位服務的可再生能源及能源儲存資產相關。
電力規模的電池儲能產業持續經歷前所未有的成長，主要由（i）全球向可再生能源轉型、（ii）對電網韌性的關注度提高、（iii）鋰電池價格下降、（iv）電力需求增加，以及（v）支持性的法規框架所驅動。
我們認為能源儲存市場由三個主要元素組成：
•能源儲存解決方案 — 零組件（包括電池）、專業服務與勞務，用以製造、組裝與安裝能源儲存系統。能源儲存解決方案市場由全球部署新的能源儲存解決方案所驅動，其可達市場由與製造、交付與安裝新能源儲存解決方案相關的年度支出組成。BloombergNEF於2025年10月20日發佈的2H 2025能源儲存市場展望中估計，全球電力規模市場（不含中國）預計在2024年至2035年間將增加約3,201 GWh。
•服務 — 能源儲存解決方案所需的定期運營與維護（"O&M"）服務，以及由第三方提供的資產管理服務，當資產所有者委外其系統運作時。服務市場元素由全球安裝的能源儲存解決方案成長所驅動，其可達市場由整個能源儲存專案羣體的定期年度服務支出組成，並持續透過新安裝而成長。

•數位應用與軟體 — 用以協助資產所有者優化其系統與組合表現的雲端軟體，包括資產表現管理（"APM"）軟體與用於資產交易應用的智能預測與投標優化軟體。雲端軟體應用可部署於能源儲存資產與可再生能源資產上。數位應用產業由安裝的能源儲存解決方案與可再生能源資產成長所驅動，其可達市場由全球安裝的能源儲存解決方案與可再生能源資產總體組成。我們認為不僅有機會在個別資產上部署數位服務與軟體解決方案，也有機會在整個能源儲存艦隊與發電資產組合上部署，以提升表現與經濟效益，同時降低資產總成本（"TCO"），透過服務生產力的提升與改善
提升預測性維護，以及透過最佳化各種資產類型來降低整個投資組合的總體碳足跡的機會。
如上所述，我們認為有許多關鍵因素驅動能源儲存產業的持續成長，包括但不限於：
•全球向可再生能源轉型：從化石燃料轉向可再生能源發電的持續過程，預期將繼續需要顯著增加的能源儲存容量，以抵消間歇性可再生能源資源可能造成的電網不穩定，並在自然資源可能無法使用時，使可再生能源發電設施產生的電力得以使用。能源儲存將在管理可再生能源電力輸出變動方面至關重要。
•電網韌性：現有電力網的容量限制正在增加，而這些電網並未設計用以支持分散式和可再生能源發電基礎設施或技術，例如電動車，這使能源儲存資產成為關鍵解決方案。

•鋰電池價格下降：產業成長及客戶持續採用能源儲存解決方案，主要由鋰電池成本下降所驅動。鋰電池儲能硬體的成本在過去十年中顯著下降，並導致今日擁有廣大的可接觸市場。在財務年度 2022 年，我們看到鋰電池價格從前幾年有所上升，不過在財務年度 2023 至 2025 年，價格已回到歷史趨勢，即每年下降，這部分歸因於製造過度供應和市場飽和，以及基礎原材料成本下降，包括鋰，以及電動車（"EV"）產業需求的減緩。能源儲存市場持續快速演進，雖然我們認為鋰電池成本將在長遠來看持續下降，但可能不會下降或下降速度不如我們預期。如果成本在長遠來看不會持續下降，而是維持穩定或上升，如財務年度 2022 年所見，這可能會對我們產品與服務的需求、營業收入、訂單量、市佔率及擴張業務的能力產生不利影響。

•電力需求增加：受到資料中心和人工智慧等因素驅動。電力需求的激增增加了對能源儲存系統的需求，以確保電網穩定、管理峯值負載並為電網提供可靠性，尤其是在電力使用高峯期。在接下來的 5 年內，需要大量部署技術解決方案以配合人工智慧資料中心的建設，而能源儲存非常適合在這個時間軸內大規模部署。根據美國能源部 2024 年 4 月的出版物，美國的電力需求預期在未來十年內大幅成長。這部分受到資料中心和人工智慧的驅動，根據美國能源部 2024 年 12 月的另一份報告，資料中心預計在 2028 年將消耗約 6.7% 到 12% 的美國總電力。我們也觀察到其他國家，包括我們營運的國家，電力需求增加的相似趨勢。

paragraphs: 下列為管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，提供管理層認為與評估及瞭解我們經審計之合併財務報表與營運成果相關之資訊，應與本年度報告書其他部分所載之財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。此討論可能包含基於目前預期之展望性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。我們實際之結果可能與這些展望性陳述所預期者有重大差異，原因包括其他重要因素，包括 Part I, Item 1A 所述之 "風險因素" 以及 "展望性資訊警示聲明" 章節，以及本年度報告書其他部分。有關我們財務狀況與營運成果自 2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度至 2023 年 9 月 30 日財務年度之變動，請參閱本年度報告書 Part II, Item 7 所述之 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析"，該部分為 2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度之 10-K 報告，於 2024 年 11 月 29 日提交至 SEC。我們過去之結果未必能代表未來任何期間之結果。

我們於 2021 年 11 月 1 日完成首次公開發行股票（IPO）及一系列組織交易（合稱為 "交易"），Fluence Energy, Inc. 成為一家控股公司，其主要資產為 Fluence Energy, LLC（"LLC Interests"）之有限責任權益。我們所有業務均透過 Fluence Energy, LLC 及其子公司進行，Fluence Energy, LLC 之財務結果已合併至我們之財務報表中。除非上下文明確另有說明，否則 "Fluence"、"我們"、"我們"、"我們" 或 "本公司" 均指 Fluence Energy, Inc. 及其全資子公司。
我們之財務年度自 10 月 1 日開始，至 9 月 30 日為止。提及 "財務年度 2023"、"財務年度 2024" 及 "財務年度 2025" 指 2023 年 9 月 30 日財務年度、2024 年 9 月 30 日財務年度及 2025 年 9 月 30 日財務年度。

我們認為，我們之表現與未來成功取決於若干因素，這些因素為我們帶來重大機會，但也伴隨風險與挑戰，包括下文所述及 Part I, Item 1A 所述之 "風險因素"。請參閱本年度報告書 Part I, Item 1 所述之 "業務" 章節之 "產業與市場機會"、"成長策略"、"製造"、"供應鏈"、"政府規範與合規" 及 "競爭" 子節，以取得有關某些關鍵因素、趨勢與不確定性對我們表現之影響之進一步討論。
任何現有或未來之訴訟、政府調查或其他監管或法律程序之結果均無法確定，且無論結果如何，我們可能因聲請、訴訟、政府調查及其他監管或法律程序而產生重大成本，並分散管理層之資源。
有關我們重大待決法律事項之描述，請參閱本年度報告書其他部分所載之 "附註 15 - 承諾與待決事項"，該附註為經審計之合併財務報表之摘要。

paragraphs: 本公司之業務、營運、財務表現及未來展望、計畫與目標，受多種風險與不確定因素影響，包括下文所述之風險，這些風險可能對本公司之業務、營運成果、財務狀況及本公司A類普通股之交易價格造成重大不利影響。請謹慎考量下文所述之風險與不確定因素，並配合本年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括第二部分第七項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」及本公司合併財務報表與相關附註，這些資訊可能對本公司之業務、營運成果、財務狀況及本公司A類普通股之交易價格造成重大影響。請參閱上方之「關於未來展望陳述之警示聲明」。
本公司之業務與客戶對本公司產品之需求，部分取決於政府對再生能源與/或儲能之激勵措施與/或相關法規，這些法規可能要求或鼓勵使用再生能源與/或儲能。政府激勵措施或法規之變更或潛在變更，已對本公司儲能解決方案之需求造成影響，未來亦可能對本公司業務、營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。

美國聯邦、州、地方及外國政府機構提供激勵措施與/或法規，要求或鼓勵再生能源與/或儲能之使用，針對再生能源與儲能產品與解決方案之所有者、最終用戶、經銷商、系統整合商與製造商，以促進再生能源與儲能之應用，形式包括回饋金、稅收抵免、其他財務激勵措施、採購要求與市場結構。這些激勵措施與法規之範圍與持續時間因管轄地區與所涉資產類型而異。本公司客戶通常使用本公司儲能解決方案於電網連接應用，電力透過電力購買協議或於組織化電力市場中銷售。政府激勵措施或法規之減少、消除、修改、到期或被判定不適用，或潛在之任何減少、消除、修改、到期或被判定不適用，已對本公司產品之競爭力、產業成長與本公司業務造成負面影響。這些政府激勵措施與/或法規可能於特定日期到期，或在資金分配完畢時終止，或因再生能源採用率提高、法律挑戰、政策或優先事項改變、新法規或法規之採納、新法規指引或時間經過而減少或終止。政府激勵措施與/或法規之減少、修改、終止或被判定不適用，可能在未預警情況下發生。這些政策、法規與激勵措施可能不會以現有形式或完全不存在。這些政府激勵措施與/或法規之減少、修改、消除、到期或潛在之任何減少、消除、修改、到期，或被判定不適用，已影響並可能未來影響客戶對本公司產品之需求，可能導致客戶流失與潛在客戶專案喪失，且已並可能未來對本公司業務、營運成果與現金流造成損害。本公司有時會追求收購或其他戰略交易，以利用潛在激勵措施。然而，任何此類收購或交易可能不會依照預期時間表完成，或完全不進行，且可能無法實現其預期效益。

例如，2022年8月，美國通過《IRA》（《投資稅額抵免法案》），包含支持採用儲能解決方案之激勵措施，包括新的「技術中立」第48E條款投資稅額抵免（「ITC」）與第45Y條款生產稅額抵免（「PTC」），對先前第48條款非「技術中立」投資稅額抵免與第45條款生產稅額抵免之變更，以及第45X條款先進製造生產稅額抵免（「AMPC」）。2025年7月4日，《OBBBA》（《美國能源儲能法案》）簽署成為法律，大幅修改《IRA》之部分條款，包括與儲能相關之條款。《OBBBA》支持美國之儲能，因該法案包含對儲能專案之ITC長期持續可用性，以及對美國製造之儲能系統電池、模組與逆變器之AMPC可用性。某些稅額抵免，特別是對儲能之ITC，將於2033年後開始逐步減少，適用於於2033年後開始建設之專案（依照美國國稅局（「IRS」）指引）。《IRA》所頒布之現行工資與學徒要求，持續適用於《OBBBA》之下，使專案所有者可獲得完整的ITC價值，且若專案所有者同時符合國內內容補貼信用與能源社區補貼信用之條件，信用價值可進一步提高。《OBBBA》修改了ITC之國內內容補貼信用條款，使專案所有者必須達到更高的最低國內內容百分比門檻。此外，《OBBBA》修改了ITC與AMPC，建立新的禁止外國實體（「PFE」）限制。

新的PFE限制適用於《IRA》下幾乎所有關鍵稅額抵免，分為兩種形式：(i) 對於2025年7月4日後開始之稅務年度，取得ITC與AMPC稅額抵免之納稅人不得為PFE；(ii) 對於2026年後開始建設之ITC專案，以及在2025年7月4日後開始之稅務年度內製造與銷售之AMPC合格零組件，ITC合格專案或AMPC合格零組件必須從非PFE取得一定比例之材料（稱為「材料協助」），且該比例每年逐步提高。《OBBBA》包含關於PFE限制符合性要求之實質細節，並要求美國財政部於2026年12月31日前發布實施規則。目前對《IRA》及相關指引、《OBBBA》及未來相關指引（包括PFE限制）之某些方面仍存在持續不確定性。過去，這種不確定性導致部分客戶花費較長時間評估、協商並簽訂儲能協議，已對本公司業務與營運成果造成影響。目前對《OBBBA》所施加之變更之不確定性，未來可能
同樣導致客戶延遲簽約決策，或導致客戶延遲或取消現有專案，因應此種不確定性，這可能對本公司業務與營運成果造成重大負面影響。
